# share.notambourine.com

Private artifact sharing. Upload a file or folder, get an unguessable branded
URL, hand it to one person. This file is the whole API.

## Auth

Writes need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: your raw vault token. Load it from
1Password by reference; never paste it into a transcript or a shell history.
Convention: it lives in your Employee vault as item `share-token`, field
`credential`. Run a command under this prefix (op run resolves the reference
from the environment; single-quote the inner command so your shell does not
expand $SHARE_TOKEN early):

    SHARE_TOKEN=op://Employee/share-token/credential op run -- sh -c '<command>'

Reads need nothing: the unguessable hash in the URL is the credential.

## Upload

    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      -F f=@out/report.html https://share.notambourine.com/up/<space>

Returns the share URL as plain text (`Accept: application/json` for JSON).
Multiple `-F f=@...` fields keep their relative paths, so a folder with an
`index.html` serves as a real page with its own CSS, JS, and images.

Query parameters:
  ttl=<dur>|forever  fixed artifact expiry, default 90d (e.g. 7d, 12h, 4w)

Nothing renders and nothing generates at upload. With
`Accept: application/json` the answer carries url, hash, expiresAt, files, and
adminUrl plus adminExp: the working-page link (see Working page), live for
5 minutes, for the uploader only - never a link to hand over. The plain-text
answer stays the one hand-over URL.

## Working page

    curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/<space>/<hash>/admin

Returns {url, exp}: the artifact's working page, live for 5 minutes. Upload
mints one too (adminUrl in its JSON answer); this route re-opens it. The url
carries ?c=<token>, a credential scoped to exactly this artifact's write routes
- it is not a view credential and never belongs in a link you hand over. It
authorizes three writes:

    POST /<space>/<hash>/generate?c=<token>  {"name":"deck","sources":["notes.md"]}
    POST /<space>/<hash>/config?c=<token>    {"ttl":"30d"} or {"ttl":"forever"}
    DELETE /<space>/<hash>/?c=<token>        same soft delete as Revoke below

The generate write composes the named sources, in the order given, into one
document through a server-side prompt. `name` is one of deck, agenda, renewal,
ship-summary; `sources` are paths this share holds, each a .md, .markdown, or
.txt. Answers 201 {path, size, bare}: the version that landed
(`deck.<epoch>.md`) and the bare name it now answers to (`deck.md`). 400 names
a bad file or name, 413 refuses a run over 200,000 bytes of text with the count
and the files, 502 means the model call failed and nothing stored, 503 means the
AI binding is absent.

The document is the only thing a generation writes; no manifest records it, so
the index page and the bare alias both find it by listing. The request holds for
the length of the model call - a few seconds - which is how the working page's
form gets away with submitting into a new tab and no polling anywhere. A form
POST (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, repeated `sources` fields) answers 303
to the version instead of the JSON above, so ask with
`Accept: application/json` to get data.

The config write answers {c, exp, expiresAt, expiry}: a fresh 5-minute token
with the epoch it dies (each edit restarts the clock; adopt the new c) plus the
expiry it committed, rendered. The ttl counts from upload; a ttl the artifact
has already outlived counts from the write instead.

Opened in a browser, the url serves the working page: the source checkboxes and
generation buttons, format links to hand over (they carry no c=), the expiry
chips, and delete. An invalid or expired c= serves the public index, never a 401.

## Index page

    curl -sS -H "Accept: application/json" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/<space>/<hash>/

The share's own root, with no credential. JSON: space, hash, createdAt,
expiresAt, uploads (path, size, stamp, exports), generations (name, versions
newest first), and renders (source, path, key, check). `stamp` is the epoch a
generated version landed under and null on an upload; `key` is which mode
rendered - slides.pdf, doc.pdf, page.pdf, page.png; `check` carries
{slides, overflow} for a deck render that was measured, where overflow lists the
1-indexed slides whose content clips the page.

In a browser the same URL is a page listing the same thing. A share whose upload
carries an `index.html` serves that page here instead: the folder is the
artifact.

## Revoke

    curl -sS -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/<space>/<hash>/

Soft delete: the upload moves to trash and purges 90 days later. The live
link dies within 10 minutes (cache lifetime).

## Viewing

The same URL renders for browsers and serves raw bytes to everything else
(curl, <img src>, Slack unfurls). Overrides: ?raw forces bytes, ?view forces
the branded shell, ?view=source shows
uploaded HTML highlighted instead of executed.

Fenced code blocks come out highlighted, and a ```mermaid fence comes out
drawn: flowchart, sequence, state, class, ER, and xychart, as inline SVG in
the brand's colors, on the page and in the PDF. A type the renderer has no
layout for (pie, gantt, mindmap) falls back to showing its own source.

Decks render with Marp. --- splits slides, and Marp directives apply:
<!-- _class: lead --> centers a title slide, <!-- paginate: true --> numbers
them. Arrow keys move between slides and the #n fragment links to one.

## Formats

Swap a share URL's extension for a branded export: uploaded `deck.md`, ask for
`deck.pdf`. A suffix decides the output on its own, so Accept gets no vote, and
a file uploaded under the suffixed name always wins over the export.

    deck.md              branded page, deck or document decided from the content
    deck.pdf             PDF, deck or document decided from the content

Both read the content to choose: `marp: true` front matter or `---` slide
separators mean deck, anything else means document. When one upload holds both
deck.md and deck.markdown, the .md spelling wins the base name.

An uploaded HTML page exports too: uploaded `page.html`, ask for

    page.pdf             PDF of the page, plain A4
    page.png             screenshot, the whole page at 1280 wide

PNG is HTML-only; markdown keeps its own family above. When one upload holds
both deck.md and deck.html, markdown wins the base and deck.png is a 404.

A generated document lands stamped (`deck.<epoch>.md`) and the bare name follows
the newest stamp, so `deck.md` and `deck.pdf` serve the latest version while
every older stamp keeps its own URL. The index page lists all of them.

Nothing renders at upload. A .pdf or .png is rendered by the first request that
asks for it and then cached, so that request can take a few seconds; one that is
not rendered yet answers 202 with Retry-After: 5 - wait that long and
re-request. It never answers HTML at 200, so `curl -o` cannot write a page into
a .pdf.

## Skill

GET /SKILL.md is a drop-in Claude skill covering both verbs.
